executiveSummary: The collected intelligence supports an assessment that the near-term maritime cyber risk environment is moderate, driven by recent port and logistics disruptions and reinforced by U.S. government guidance on navigation integrity and vessel cybersecurity during inactivity. Confidence: medium-high.

sectors: Ports and Terminals (North Carolina Ports Authority)
Logistics and Warehousing (CEVA Logistics, CMA CGM group)
Vessel Owners/Operators (USCG MTSA applicability for inactive/laid-up vessels)
Bridge Teams / Navigation (GPS interference and AIS spoofing advisory)

keyFindings: Port operations disruption: North Carolina Ports experienced a confirmed cyberattack causing IT outages and slowed gate operations across multiple facilities; navigation impact not reported. View Article
Supply-chain continuity risk: CEVA Logistics reported Europe-based warehousing disruptions, indicating upstream/downstream effects on carrier schedules and cargo readiness. View Article

Compliance signal: USCG MSIB 04-26 clarifies MTSA cybersecurity applicability to laid-up/inactive vessels, highlighting the need to maintain controls, monitoring, and response readiness during nonoperational periods. Government Advisory
Navigation integrity remains at risk from GPS interference and AIS spoofing; bridge teams should cross-validate with independent sensors and visual/radar fixes. Maritime Advisory
No new CVE-driven maritime OT exploit reporting is present in this set; defensive focus should remain on access control, segmentation, and incident containment at the IT/OT boundary.

descriptions: Operational disruption of enterprise IT systems (ports, logistics) leading to service slowdowns.
Standing navigation-data integrity risks (GPS interference; AIS spoofability) per government advisory.

outlook72h: Analysts should monitor for continuing recovery and customer notifications regarding the North Carolina Ports and CEVA Logistics disruptions. Confidence: medium. Port Incident Logistics Incident Additional compliance and implementation questions may surface as operators interpret USCG MSIB 04-26 for fleet lay-up plans and audits. Confidence: high. Government Advisory Navigation integrity risk remains situationally elevated in regions experiencing GPS interference; crews should apply cross-check procedures. Confidence: medium.
